'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Islamist insurgency in the Sahel]]
**[[French military withdrawal from West Africa (2022–present)|French military withdrawal from West Africa]]
***[[President of France|French President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] says [[France]] was right to intervene militarily in the [[Africa]]n [[Sahel]] against the [[mujahideen]], that he is still waiting for the Sahel states to thank France and that the [[French Armed Forces]] were not forced out. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/still-awaiting-thanks-stopping-islamists-sahel-macron-says-2025-01-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**[[Gaza war]], [[Israeli incursions in the West Bank (2023–present)|Israeli incursions in the West Bank]]
***[[2025 al-Funduq shooting]]
****Three [[Israelis]] are killed and eight others are injured in a [[mass shooting]] by [[Palestinian political violence|Palestinian gunmen]] firing at a bus and two vehicles on [[Highway 55 (Israel)|Highway 55]] in [[Al-Funduq]] in the [[West Bank]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cdjgv1r4x81o (BBC News)]
*[[Naxalite–Maoist insurgency]]
**[[2025 Bijapur Naxal attack]]
***A bomb blast attributed to [[Communist Party of India (Maoist)|Maoist rebels]] in [[Bijapur district, Chhattisgarh|Bijapur]], [[Chhattisgarh]], [[India]], kills eight [[Indian Police Service|police]] officers and a driver traveling in a police vehicle. [https://www.reuters.com/world/india/ten-policemen-feared-killed-bomb-blast-central-india-tv-report-says-2025-01-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Kherson strikes (2022–present)|Kherson strikes]], [[Attacks on civilians in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***A [[Russia]]n [[drone warfare|drone attack]]s a civilian passenger bus in [[Kherson]], [[Ukraine]], reportedly killing at least one person and injuring at least nine others. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-drone-kills-one-injures-nine-passenger-bus-ukraines-kherson-2025-01-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[2024 Magdeburg car attack]]
**The death toll in the [[vehicle-ramming attack]] at the [[Magdeburg Christmas market]] in [[Magdeburg]], [[Germany]], on December 20, increases to six after a 52-year-old woman dies from injuries sustained in the attack. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cql5nlrp374o (BBC News)]
*[[List of North Korean missile tests|North Korean missile tests]]
**The [[South Korea]]n [[Republic of Korea Armed Forces|military]] reports that [[Korean People's Army|North Korea]] has fired what appears to be an [[intermediate-range ballistic missile]] toward the [[Sea of Japan]], in what would be [[North Korea|the country]]'s first missile launch in two months. The launch comes as [[U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Antony Blinken]] visits [[Seoul]], South Korea, for talks with South Korean leaders. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crrwyv75g5xo (BBC News)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**At least eight gunmen are killed and three [[Federal Police (Mexico)|policemen]] are wounded after security agents repels an attack near the Buenavista de Libertad, [[Yuriria]], [[Guanajuato]], [[Mexico]]. Security forces members seize four vehicles, ballistic vests, and twelve firearms. In the same area, another encounter was reported two months ago, leaving three officers wounded. [https://www.proceso.com.mx/nacional/estados/2025/1/6/fuerzas-de-seguridad-abaten-ocho-presuntos-criminales-en-yuriria-guanajuato-343294.html (''Revista Proceso'')]
*Two people are killed and two others are injured in an [[improvised explosive device|IED]] attack at a school near [[Abuja]], [[Nigeria]], with [[Nigeria Police Force|police]] identifying three men as suspects in bringing the device to the site. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/suspected-bomb-explosion-kills-two-people-nigerian-school-police-say-2025-01-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2022–2023 Russia–European Union gas dispute]]
**According to [[Slovakia]], a planned meeting between Slovak, [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]], and [[European Commission]] officials over gas supplies scheduled for Tuesday has been cancelled due to Ukraine's refusal to participate in the meeting. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/slovakia-says-gas-supply-meeting-with-ukraine-european-commission-cancelled-2025-01-06/ (Reuters)]
*The [[Politics of Brazil|Brazilian government]] announces that [[Indonesia]] has joined the [[BRICS]] [[trade bloc]] as a full member. [https://www.reuters.com/world/indonesia-join-brics-bloc-full-member-brazil-says-2025-01-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[Colombia]]n bank [[Davivienda]] and [[Canada|Canadian]] bank [[Scotiabank]] announces a [[mergers and acquisitions|merger]] where Davivienda will absorb Scotiabank's operations in Colombia, [[Costa Rica]] and [[Panama]], and, Scotiabank will acquire 20% of Davidienda's stakes. [https://www.scotiabank.com/corporate/en/home/media-centre/media-centre/news-release.html.html?id=4186&language=en (Scotiabank)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Assam mine incident]]
**Several miners are trapped in a [[coal mine]] in [[Dima Hasao district|Dima Hasao]], [[Assam]], India, with rescue efforts underway involving the [[State Disaster Response Force (Assam)|State Disaster Response Force]], the [[National Disaster Response Force]], and the [[Indian Army]]. Local authorities state that flooding may have caused the incident. [https://www.reuters.com/world/india/several-miners-trapped-coal-mine-indias-assam-2025-01-06/ (Reuters)]
*18 people are killed in a multi-vehicle collision on [[Van Reenen's Pass]] in [[KwaZulu-Natal]], [[South Africa]]. [https://www.enca.com/news/18-killed-multi-vehicle-crash-van-reenens-pass (ENCA)]

**The [[United States]] reports its first death from [[H5N1]] bird flu after a man died in the hospital in [[Louisiana]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/louisiana-reports-first-bird-flu-related-death-us-state-agency-says-2025-01-06/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Humanitarian aid during the Syrian civil war]]
***The [[International Committee of the Red Cross]] announces plans to expand its operations in [[Syria]] beyond an initial [[United States dollar|US$]]100 million program, citing urgent needs in the [[Health in Syria|health]], [[Water supply and sanitation in Syria|water]], and [[Energy in Syria|power sectors]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/icrc-expand-syria-humanitarian-efforts-beyond-100-mln-programme-2025-01-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[International reactions to the 2024 Venezuelan presidential election]], [[Paraguay–Venezuela relations]]
**The [[Venezuela]]n government suspends diplomatic relations with [[Paraguay]], after [[President of Paraguay|Paraguayan President]] [[Santiago Peña]] recognizes [[Edmundo González]] as [[President of Venezuela|president-elect of Venezuela]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/venezuela-breaks-diplomatic-relations-with-paraguay-2025-01-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Volksverhetzung]]
**[[Germany]] reports a significant increase in [[Far-right politics|far-right]] crime, primarily from increasing [[Online hate speech|online expression offenses]] and [[hate speech]], as well as an increase in [[Gaza war]]-related resentment. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/germany-sees-rise-far-right-crime-with-online-offences-main-driver-2025-01-06/ (Reuters)]
*The [[Court of Appeal of Malaysia]] orders a [[Judiciary of Malaysia|lower court]] to reconsider former [[Prime Minister of Malaysia|Prime Minister]] [[Najib Razak]]'s claim of a royal order granting him [[home detention]], which he alleges was issued alongside his reduced prison sentence for his involvement in the [[1MDB corruption scandal]]. The ruling follows the disclosure of a letter confirming the existence of such an order, which the [[Government of Malaysia|government]] asserts they have not received. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/malaysia-court-grants-jailed-ex-pm-najibs-request-see-document-he-says-allows-2025-01-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[Ministry of Interior, Justice and Peace (Venezuela)|Venezuelan Interior Minister]] [[Diosdado Cabello]] says that 125 foreign citizens have been arrested on suspicion of serving as [[United States]] [[mercenaries]] in order to cause a [[coup]] in Venezuela. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/venezuela-says-125-foreigners-including-one-israeli-arrested-on-suspicion-of-being-us-mercenaries/ (''The Times of Israel'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 Austrian legislative election]]
**After the [[Austrian People's Party]] fails to form a government, [[President of Austria]] [[Alexander van der Bellen]] gives the mandate to form a [[2024 Austrian legislative election|post-election]] government to the [[Freedom Party of Austria|Freedom Party]]'s leader [[Herbert Kickl]], who is expected to rule within a coalition of the two parties. [https://www.dw.com/de/van-der-bellen-erteilt-fp%C3%B6-auftrag-zur-regierungsbildung/a-71227474 (DW)]
*[[Conscription in Israel]], [[Exemption from military service in Israel]]
**More than 50 [[Haredi Judaism|Haredi Jews]] join the [[Israel Defense Forces]] for the first time since the start of the [[Gaza war]], forming the Haredi [[Hasmonean Brigade]], after repeated protests against the [[conscription of yeshiva students]]. [https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/us/israel-defense-forces-recruit-first-ultra-orthodox-soldiers-for-hasmonean-brigade/articleshow/117000437.cms?from=mdr (''The Economic Times'')]
*[[Proposals for the United States to purchase Greenland]]
**The [[Frederik X|King of Denmark]] officially changes the [[Coat of arms of Denmark|Danish coat of arms]] to feature [[Greenland]] and the [[Faroe Islands]] more prominently, following suggestions from [[United States]] [[President-elect of the United States|president-elect]] [[Donald Trump]] about the nation purchasing Greenland. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/jan/06/danish-king-changes-coat-of-arms-in-apparent-rebuke-to-donald-trump (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Resignation of Justin Trudeau]]
**[[Prime Minister of Canada|Canadian Prime Minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]] announces his resignation as leader of the [[Liberal Party of Canada|Liberal Party]] and also announces that he will resign as Prime Minister once [[2025 Liberal Party of Canada leadership election|a new Liberal Party leader is chosen]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/clyjmy7vl64t (BBC News)]
*[[Second presidential transition of Donald Trump]]
**The [[United States Congress|U.S. Congress]] [[2025 United States Electoral College vote count|certifies]] the results of the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 presidential election]]. [[Vice President of the United States|U.S. Vice President]] and [[Kamala Harris 2024 presidential campaign|Democratic Party candidate]] in the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 presidential election]]. [[Kamala Harris]] presides over the ceremony and certifies her defeat, officially making [[Donald Trump]] the [[President-elect of the United States|President-elect]] and [[JD Vance]] the [[Vice President–elect of the United States|Vice President-elect]]. Trump and Vance are expected to be sworn-in on [[Second inauguration of Donald Trump|January 20]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/congress-meets-certify-trumps-2024-election-victory/story?id=117380065 (ABC News)]
*[[Pope Francis]] appoints Sister [[Simona Brambilla]] as Prefect of the [[Dicastery for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life]], becoming the [[Vatican City|Vatican]]'s first female prefect of the [[Roman Curia]]. [https://www.vaticannews.va/en/pope/news/2025-01/vatican-first-female-prefect-simona-brambilla-consecrated-life.html (Vatican News)]
*The [[President of São Tomé and Príncipe]], [[Carlos Vila Nova]], dismisses the Government of [[Prime Minister of São Tomé and Príncipe|Prime Minister]] [[Patrice Trovoada]]. [https://www.africanews.com/2025/01/06/sao-tome-and-principe-president-dismisses-government-by-decree/ (Africa News)]
